name: Knowledge

subjectOf.text: A single powerful application such as Google already exercises substantial control over human knowledge and thought, and could control societal outcomes by making disparate recommendations to similarly situated users.
subjectOf.abstract: For example, a powerful application such as Google has already a lot of control over human knowledge and thought.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Systems Can Upgrade AI (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808867
scope_conditions: dominant internet based applications accumulating societal functions since the early 2010s

subjectOf.text: Yi et al. (2026) report that an imperfect external verifier drives the model toward the verifier's own knowledge center.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The finding is prior work cited by the paper and is not measured in this study.
It is a limit on verifier-based selection generally, including the pool under test.
